Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (NimbleHealth ML Lead), Ethan Ross (Infra), Maya Li (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Weekly POC sync for low-precision experiments (mix of INT8/FP8).
- Reviewed benchmark deltas: throughput improved ~1.8x on INT8, FP8 shows smaller perf gain but different SNR tradeoffs.

- Next steps: share updated bench CSV, run focused regressions, schedule dedicated performance run, align rollback thresholds.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Ava: Okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the weekly mixbench retune checkin for the NimbleHealth POC. Uh if you can quick intro — Priya, Ethan, Maya?
[00:10] Priya: hi yeah Priya here, ML lead. We ran the batch from last week, had some surprises in the conversational set.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan, infra, I'll cover the peering and the KV cache warmup logs.
[00:18] Maya: Maya for product, mostly listening and tracking acceptance criteria.
[00:22] Liam: Liam from Redwood, SE. I have the new INT8/FP8 mixbench results and a couple notes on quant recipe changes.

[00:30] Ava: Cool, quick agenda — results review, triage regressions, tuning knobs, and agree next steps. Liam, do you want to kick off with the perf numbers?
[00:37] Liam: Yeah sure, uh so headline: on our hosted clusters we saw INT8 delivering about 1.7–1.9x token throughput for median latencies at 512 tokens. FP8 was more nuanced — overall throughput ~1.3x but lower variance on long sequences. However FP8 shows slightly higher SNR drop on our summarization prompts.
[01:05] Priya: When you say SNR drop, like how much magnitude? Our acceptance threshold was set to 0.02 average BLEU-like delta, right?
[01:12] Liam: Right, in our internal SNR-ish metric we saw a mean delta of 0.018 for INT8, but FP8 had pockets where it went to 0.028 on the long-convo set — so above your threshold. But other workloads (completion style) were within bounds.
[01:30] Priya: okay that matches what we saw, the conversational templates with system prompts and long context were the worst.

[01:40] Ethan: One log note — we noticed KV cache fill patterns were different with the FP8 runtime; warmup wasn't stable unless we pre-warmed the cache with typical conversational prefixes. Might be a routing/packing difference in the runtime, maybe the kernel scheduling.
[02:02] Liam: Yep that's likely — the low-precision kernel path currently changes attention tiling slightly, which affects when KV pages hit. We flagged that in the last github ticket but haven't pushed the scheduling tweak.

[02:25] Maya: From product side, the main ask is we need clear rollout rules: if regression > threshold on the priority prompt set, automatic fallback to FP16 or to a higher precision variant, and an alert to the SRE. Can Redwood do auto-fallback?
[02:40] Ava: We do. Redwood has a routing policy and can fallback to a pinned FP16 variant or to a repo-backed compatible model variant. We can also trigger a canary rollback. Liam, quick on config?
[02:50] Liam: Yeah routing policy supports per-route SNR gates, but we need the exact metric and threshold from you to wire into the rollout. Also note that fallback has perf cost — you'll lose the INT8 throughput gains.

[03:10] Priya: We're also concerned about noise from production traffic vs bench. Is Redwood's mixbench representative enough? We used some smaller in-house prompts.
[03:18] Liam: Good point. Our mixbench tries to mimic your production distribution if you share logs (PII redacted). We used the dataset you gave last month but we also appended synthetic longer dialogs.
[03:30] Priya: We can share a fresh 24h sample redacted, but we want to keep the conversational template core.

[03:44] Ethan: On infra — for the Dedicated run we suggested a 30-minute warmup with live traffic replay to populate KV cache and measure steady-state. We'll need a VPC peering window, we can do that next Tuesday in the maintenance window.
[03:59] Ava: Sounds good. We'll schedule that.

[04:05] Liam: Back to regression cluster: the set where FP8 goes over SNR threshold is mostly templates 17–23 in the regression sheet, long context + few-shot. My hypothesis: FP8 quantization amplifies softmax saturation for long K/V sequences leading to subtle rank shifts. That shows as hallucination in some completions.
[04:30] Priya: yes, we saw hallucination on case 19 — the entity swap. It's repeatable between runs which worries us.
[04:38] Liam: If it's repeatable we can try these immediate mitigations: 1) prefix-based KV pre-warm for the route, 2) micro-batching changes (smaller per-device batch) which affects kernel tiling, 3) hybrid precision for attention layers (keep attention in FP16).
[04:55] Maya: Hybrid precision sounds promising but is it supported in the POC run?
[05:00] Liam: We can do hybrid as a model variant — it's a little extra work to prepare the variant and test. Turnaround maybe 5 business days.

[05:10] Priya: And what about cost? Hybrid will reduce throughput but might avoid rollbacks. We need delta estimates.
[05:18] Ava: I'll send a pricing comparison: Hosted INT8 route vs Hosted FP8 vs Hybrid vs Dedicated INT8 with reserved capacity. We'll break down tokens per second and unit cost.

[05:30] Ethan: Security gating — for onprem/Dedicated test we need to validate KMS and SAML SSO flows. I saw a note about KMS earlier. Any blockers?
[05:40] Liam: KMS integration is standard, but if you want HSM-backed keys we have a security doc we can share. On SAML, Redwood Console (sometimes transcribed as Consool) integrates with SSO, should be straightforward.

[05:55] Priya: Great. One more performance nuance — FP8 looked more stable on long sequences but worse on few-shot classification where weights distribution matter. Could we run a focused few-shot bench?
[06:08] Liam: Yep we can add a 50-case few-shot regression set — Priya if you can pick the 50 prompts we will run on both FP8 and INT8 and produce per-case diffs.
[06:20] Priya: Will do, I'll upload to the shared folder after this call.

[06:28] Ava: Cool. Any blockers for the Dedicated run schedule? Ethan?
[06:33] Ethan: Peering window tentatively fine, I'll confirm the exact IP ranges by Friday. Also want to test warmup script — Liam, do you have a warmup suggestion?
[06:42] Liam: Yeah run a 30-minute replay with 10qps steady load including the typical prefixes. That should fill KV and reach steady token throughput. We can instrument token-level latencies.

[06:57] Maya: For acceptance criteria — define SNR threshold and allowed rollback frequency per week. I propose we set the SNR delta cutoff to 0.025 for the conversational set and allow at most one rollback-triggering incident per week before manual review. Thoughts?
[07:12] Priya: 0.025 aligns with our risk tolerance.
[07:15] Ava: We'll wire that into the routing policy as the gate; Liam will need the exact list of prompts and owners.

[07:25] Liam: Quick note — we saw a small end-to-end latency increase on INT8 for very short prompts: cold start overhead is slightly higher because of kernel selection overhead. It's in the noise but worth noting.
[07:40] Priya: Interesting, that might affect micro-interactions. We'll flag it.

[07:45] Ava: Ok recap and next steps. Liam, you'll produce the updated mixbench CSV with per-case diffs and the hybrid variant ETA.
[07:54] Liam: Yep, I'll put files in the shared folder by Monday 2026-07-12.
[07:58] Ava: Priya will run the 50-case few-shot and the 50-case conv regression on FP8 and upload results.
[08:04] Priya: Yes, due 2026-07-15.
[08:07] Ava: Ethan will confirm VPC peering and KMS specifics by 2026-07-14.
[08:12] Ethan: Confirmed I will.
[08:14] Maya: I'll draft acceptance criteria doc with the SNR threshold and rollback cadence and share for signature.
[08:20] Ava: Great. Any final questions?
[08:24] Priya: um no, that's it. Thanks.
[08:26] Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the sheet and Slack thread.

(End of recording)
